source.title: CE-Bench: Towards a Reliable Contrastive Evaluation Benchmark of Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: A. Gul'ko; Yusen Peng; Sachin Kumar

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates sparse-autoencoder interpretability, but does not test whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs or how often neurons are polysemantic.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many SAE-level benchmark comparisons and a sample of neuron-wise activation scores. The benchmark comparisons are not results about the claim's specified polysemanticity measures. The sample is recorded as a related activation-pattern finding, but it does not establish whether a neuron has one coherent job or unrelated mixed responses.
record.test_reason: CE-Bench evaluates SAE interpretability with LLM-free contrastive scores on Gemma-2-2B SAEs. It measures no neuron's response to unrelated inputs and no share of polysemantic neurons in a base model. The width result (Fig. 3) is an SAE-level interpretability score; the authors only interpret it as resolving polysemanticity. It does not measure polysemanticity itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that CE-Bench is a reproducible, LLM-free SAE interpretability benchmark aligning with SAEBench (Spearman about 0.71, CRPR 77.3%). They also report that top-k and p-anneal SAEs, wider SAEs and middle layers score highest. They mention polysemanticity only as an interpretation of the width trend.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates pretrained SAEs with contrastive story pairs and SAE-level interpretability metrics; it does not use the original sources' neuron-focused methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that SAE-level benchmark scores vary with pooling strategy and the sparsity penalty setting; these are not measurements of polysemantic-neuron prevalence.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2-2B JumpReLU SAEs, wider latent spaces (4k, 16k, 65k) gave higher CE-Bench interpretability scores. The authors read this as wider SAEs reducing polysemanticity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider SAE dictionaries yield higher contrastive-activation interpretability scores for SAE latents.

fits_no_version.finding: For one example story pair, only a small subset of SAE latents had high contrastive or independence scores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subject-specific contrastive signal in SAE latents is concentrated in few latents.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The authors state that the dataset is synthetic and may favor GPT-4's stylistic and semantic regularities, and that its domain coverage is limited. The neuron-wise example is one story pair and does not directly assess polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: SAE-level architecture, width, layer, pooling, and benchmark-alignment results were not included because they report interpretability scores or correlations rather than individual-neuron polysemanticity.

untested.parts: No count of polysemantic MLP neurons in LLMs, and no layer comparison on that measure. The layer-depth and layer-type results are SAE-level scores.
There is no feature-count vs neuron-count manipulation. The SAE width trend is only interpreted as reducing polysemanticity; it is not measured.
Only SAE architectures are compared, using a contrastive interpretability score. The polysemantic share of model neurons is not measured, and neither is any performance cost.
The pooling ablation concerns aggregation of an SAE-level benchmark score, not classification of individual neurons as polysemantic.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Polysemanticity is invoked only interpretively, in the Section 4.3 / Fig. 3 caption, and is not measured. Rows r1 and r2 are illustrations of the metric.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test mixed responses in image classifiers such as InceptionV1.
Does not estimate the share of polysemantic MLP neurons in transformer language models or compare layers on that measure.
The width experiment does not measure feature count relative to neuron count, capacity pressure, or polysemanticity directly.
Does not test polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Compares SAE architectures and widths using SAE-level interpretability scores, not the share of polysemantic neurons or performance costs of reducing that share.
Does not investigate whether apparently mixed neurons detect a shared feature or related offshoots of one job.
Compares aggregation strategies for SAE-level scores, not whether neuron polysemanticity depends on activation range or explanation scoring.

rows.subject: JumpReLU SAE probing Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Computed neuron-wise contrastive scores for the first contrastive story pair.

conditions.value: first pair in the curated dataset

rows.measure: Neuron-wise contrastive score; maximum over neurons used as the SAE contrastive score
rows.value: The paper reports that only a small subset of neurons had high scores and most clustered near the origin; the highest contrastive score was 109.2734.
rows.note: This measures differential responses to a designed contrastive story pair, not whether the neuron responds to unrelated inputs.
rows.check: The 'neurons' are SAE latents, not model MLP neurons. The value is the max contrastive score for one story pair, about a single subject. It cannot show responses to unrelated inputs. Arguably this is an illustration of the metric rather than a result.

rows.subject: JumpReLU SAE probing Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Computed neuron-wise independence scores for the first contrastive story pair.

conditions.value: first pair in the curated dataset

rows.measure: Neuron-wise independence score; maximum over neurons used as the SAE independence score
rows.value: The paper reports that only a small subset of neurons had high scores and most clustered near the origin; the highest independence score was 195.9004.
rows.note: The score measures deviation from a dataset-wide activation average, not whether a neuron has one coherent job.
rows.check: Same issue as r1: the units are SAE latents, and the value is the max independence score for one example pair. It does not bear on polysemanticity.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
